brief: Build the admin back office of an online store. Pages (each one is a route): (1) a dashboard with six KPI tiles (revenue, orders, average order value, new customers, refunds, low-stock items), a sales-by-day bar list, a top-products table and a recent-activity feed; (2) a product catalog with a search box, a category filter, a status filter, a sortable table and pagination; (3) a product detail page with tabs (overview, variants, pricing, media) where each tab is its own form section, and a delete-confirmation dialog; (4) a create-product page with a validated multi-section form (basic info, pricing, inventory, shipping); (5) an orders list with status tabs that show counts, a date-range filter and a bulk-action bar; (6) an order detail page with the line items, a payment summary, a shipping-address card, a status timeline, a refund dialog and an internal-notes panel; (7) a customers list with search and a segment filter; (8) a customer detail page with a profile card, an order-history table, lifetime-value stats and a tags editor; (9) an inventory page with a low-stock alert banner, a per-warehouse stock table and an adjust-stock dialog with a reason field; (10) a reports page with a period selector, a revenue summary, a category breakdown and an export button that shows a success notice; (11) a settings page with tabs for store profile, tax rates (an editable list), shipping zones (an editable list) and staff accounts (invite dialog, role select). Shared pieces: an app shell with a sidebar navigation and a top bar, breadcrumbs, a page header with actions, a reusable data table, pagination, a search input, a status badge, empty, loading and error states, a confirm dialog and a toast notice. Keep all data in in-memory data modules with async functions (products, orders, customers, inventory, reports, settings) so they can later be replaced by a real API. How to build it: this is a large app, so it must be split into many small components (at least 60, each one small and focused; views stay thin and only compose components). Compose pages from component contracts: use brain_map (with its filters) and brain_card to learn what a component takes and emits, and never read whole large files to use a component. If a component grows too large, split it (brain_split). Done means brain_doctor exits 0 with every page present.
